Deep risk management expertise , including third-party risk assessments, contract governance, and mitigation strategies within multi-jurisdictional environments. <p>This role assists in the oversight of all workstreams and helps to co-ordinate the delivery of projects from start to finish, working with our internal teams and local market colleagues to deliver excellence in execution.</p> <p>RESPONSIBILITIES</p> <p>Work with the OpenDoor and WPP network will be a key part of your day-to-day and enabling best practice and on-time delivery is critical.</p> reports)</li> <li>Support the finance billing process to collate PO’s, update budget trackers, and monitor client billing</li> <li>Support in ensuring client and internal Status meetings are well prepared</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skills and Experience</strong></p> <ul> <li>Excellent organization and project planning skills.</li> <li>Strong analytical skills and a data-driven mindset.</li> <li>Excellent communication and collaboration skills.</li> <li>Passion for innovation and a desire to challenge industry norms.</li> <li>Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.</li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="none">Life at WPP Media & Benefits</span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">Our passion for shaping the next era of media is powered by our commitment to</span><span data-contrast="none"> </span><span data-contrast="none">Be Extraordinary, investing in our employees to inspire transformational creativity. This commitment allows WPP Media employees to leverage the extensive global WPP Media & WPP networks to pursue their passions, build vital professional connections, and learn at the cutting edge of marketing and advertising.</span><span data-contrast="none"> </span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">We</span><span data-contrast="none"> </span><span data-contrast="none">Create an Open environment</span><span data-contrast="none"> </span><span data-contrast="none">built on trust and respect, where everyone feels they belong and has opportunities to progress. developing – every day, every campaign and every project is different which will help unleash your potential.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Measures of success</strong></p> <p><strong>In 3 months, you would have: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Got to grips with the whole booking to billing process for digital campaigns.</li> <li>Confidently created client campaign reports and understand the data validation.</li> account.</li> <li>Worked and contributed to team projects to make agency workflow more efficient.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li>Owning operational business tasks financial reconciliation of digital campaign activity.</li> <li>Proactively managing financial queries to resolution.</li> <li>Working collaboratively with the rest of the team to proactively find solutions.</li> <li>Building positive working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skills and Experience</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience within an Operations or Account / Campaign Management function (ideally with knowledge of trafficking processes, including pixels and tags) is preferential, but not essential.</li> <li>Use of Excel and capability to analyse complex data sets.</li> <li>Strong interpersonal and relationship building skills, with the ability to train others.</li> <li>Process-driven with solutions focused mind-set and a customer-centric attitude.</li> <li>Good at problem solving, with the ability to resolve issues in a timely manner.</li> <li>Team player who motivates others and encourages close collaboration.</li> stakeholder expectations.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About WPP Media</strong></p> <p>Our passion for shaping the next era of media is powered by our commitment to Be Extraordinary, investing in our This commitment allows WPP Media employees to leverage the extensive global WPP Media & WPP networks to pursue their passions, build vital professional connections, and learn at the cutting edge of marketing and advertising. </p> <p>We Create an Open environment built on trust and respect, where everyone feels they belong and has opportunities to progress. And that’s why we’ve built <strong>OpenDoor </strong>for<strong> Amazon</strong>.</p> <p><strong>OpenDoor</strong> is a unique integration of the best of WPP and Amazon – building on their respective strengths and visions. Whether at WPP or at Amazon, every project is an OpenDoor on new possibilities. Anything and everything can be an opportunity for our people to drive <em>impact</em> – for them to innovate, learn, thrive, and occasionally fail too.</p> <p>The OpenDoor partnership model is designed to deliver next-level productivity through an industry-leading approach to people, platforms and processes. OpenDoor brings together WPP agencies and disciplines including media, business consultancy, communications and brand strategy, technology and commerce, public relations and production.</p> <p>OpenDoor’s values draw on Amazon’s <a href="https://www.amazon.jobs/content/en/our-workplace/leadership-principles"><strong>16 Leadership Principles</strong></a> and WPP’s values of Open, Optimistic and Extraordinary. Together, WPP’s creative transformation and Amazon’s customer focus empower our people to challenge today’s conventions and build a better future.</p> <p>By joining OpenDoor, you will become part of a cross-functional team partnering with one of WPP’s top five global clients. This full-time, London-based role reports to the Regional Client Associate Director and supports XCM, Amazon’s Cross-Channel Marketing division. The position sits within a regional team that works remotely across the UK and Germany, with the line manager based in DE and regular collaboration with colleagues and local market teams across Europe. The Client Senior Executive coordinates campaigns and workstreams from briefing to delivery, helping to ensure consistent client service, robust operations and high-quality execution.</p> <p>XCM is Amazon’s Cross-Channel Marketing division, delivering communications for Amazon.com, including major campaigns such as Black Friday and Prime Day. OpenDoor is XCM’s media partner worldwide, excluding North America and Latin America. As Europe is the largest region supported by the WPP team, the Regional XCM Client Senior Executive plays an important role in coordinating consistent delivery across markets.</p> <p>RESPONSIBILITIES</p> <p>Collaboration across OpenDoor and the wider WPP network is central to the role, with a strong focus on best practice, operational consistency and on-time delivery.</p> <ul> wider WPP partners, working effectively across locations and time zones.</li> <li>Develop a strong understanding of Amazon’s ways of working and the OpenDoor operating model to improve organisation, quality and consistency.</li> <li>Identify and share best-in-class work from across the network, helping regional clients and local markets adopt effective approaches.</li> <li>Contribute to a positive, collaborative team environment and work with the line manager to set objectives aligned with the role and agency vision.</li> </ul> <p>QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE</p> <ul> <li>2–3 years’ experience in media planning, client management or account coordination, preferably within a network agency.</li> <li>Excellent organisational and project planning skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.</li> <li>Strong analytical skills and a data-driven mindset, with close attention to detail.</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to manage stakeholders and collaborate effectively.</li> <li>Awareness of the media and marketing industry, including key channels, emerging trends and planning principles.</li> <li>Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic and geographically distributed working environment.</li> <li>Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint and Excel.</li> <li>Ability to manage defined tasks independently and present outputs directly to clients or package them clearly for the wider team.</li> </ul> <p>BONUS POINTS</p> <ul> <li>Experience supporting and Leadership Principles.</li> <li>Understanding of cross-channel media planning and how individual channels contribute to an integrated plan.</li> </ul> <p>BENEFITS OF OPENDOOR</p> <ul> VML, part of WPP, supports WPP Enterprise Solutions by helping brands activate transformation through creativity and experience.</p></div><p><strong>Solution Architect (Permanent) </strong>with commerce experience wanted to join our Solution Archtiecture team, here at VML Enterprise Solutions </p> <p><strong>The opportunity:</strong></p> <p>A Solution Architect is required for a high-profile role giving the successful applicant the chance to lead the solution architecture for some of the world’s largest online brands and retailers and be an integral part of our talented and expanding Solution Architecture team.</p> <p>You will be responsible for creating and assuring solution architecture using a wide range of technologies, from SaaS eCommerce platforms through to client-specific cloud solutions. You’ll develop relationships with key client-side stakeholders in charge of IT and digital strategy and architecture, and you’ll work closely with our internal delivery teams to ensure your architecture vision is realised</p> <p>Our Solution Architecture team not only focus on delivery but also work with our clients in delivering the best consulting advice to ensure world class solutions that enable our clients to transact more digitally.</p> <p><strong>What you’ll be doing:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Working on large-scale digital transformation programmes with global clients, designing solutions for all the opportunity and complexity this brings</li> <li>Own the solution architecture, document it, and communicate that architecture to a wide range of audiences</li> <li>See out and considerations for a distributed eCommerce architecture and apply this knowledge to your solutions</li> <li>Understand the level at which solution architecture applies, and help transition your solutions to application and cloud architects and technical leads</li> <li>Make and justify key architectural decisions considering all relevant constraints</li> <li>Follow the principles and guidance against industry trends.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What we want from you: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Core understanding of the capabilities of a wide range of technologies typically found within an eCommerce landscape, including enterprise eCommerce platforms and components, and apply this knowledge to your solutions</li> <li>Proven experience of solution ownership,</li> <li>Experience delivering solution transformations, roadmaps and (or) Integration strategies</li> <li>Understand the capabilities of public cloud platforms and be an advocate of cloud-native solutions</li> <li>Proven experience Designing quality solutions, often large scale and transactional in nature, for global enterprise clients</li> <li>Be client and delivery focussed, able to adapt a solution to meet additional requirements and constraints and apply pragmatism when required</li> <li>Prior experience running design workshops </li> <li>Strong stakeholder management skills </li> <li>Have excellent communication, presentation and documentation skills</li> </ul> <p><strong>If you know some of this, even better:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with OMS</li> <li>Experience with PIM</li> We’ll empower you to make a difference, allow you to be yourself, and respect who you are.</p> <p><strong>Permanent only:</strong></p> <p>We offer a great benefits package including a discretionary bonus scheme, training opportunities, competitive pension, medical insurance, life assurance, social events, opportunities to buy and sell holidays, family friendly policies, discounts with hundreds of retailers and much more.</p> <p>Our personality and behaviours: We believe that we are what we do, not just what we say. That’s why we look for people who go beyond and always push our thinking to be better than yesterday.</p> <p><strong>About VML Enterprise Solutions:</strong></p> <p>Welcome to VML Enterprise Solutions, a multi-award-winning powerhouse of innovation, creativity and growth through technology in an ever-evolving world.</p> <p>Over 7,000 employees across VML’s global offices support VML Enterprise Solutions by helping to create and deliver digital transformations, Artificial Intelligence applications and technology solutions that introduce new operational efficiencies to organisations around the world.</p> <p>Our mission is to inspire global audiences to embrace and advance the world of online and offline shopping through seamless digital experiences and tech innovation. title: Staff Software Engineer (Onboard Services)
description: UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable. Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia. UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems. About the role The Staff Software Engineer (Onboard Services) will design, build, and operate the software services that run on UFORCE’s uncrewed vehicles — spanning video streaming, telemetry, autonomy integration, vehicle control, health monitoring, navigation, and device integrations. You will turn independently evolved services into one secure, testable, and maintainable onboard platform. This is a hands-on software engineering role focused on production Python services, service architecture, messaging, and reliable operation on constrained Linux hardware, including Raspberry Pi, x86, and NVIDIA Jetson. You will also own the boundary between the vehicle and the backend: clear, versioned contracts with cloud services, deployment systems, video infrastructure, and operator interfaces that work over intermittent, low-bandwidth links. Working with backend, autonomy, hardware, QA, and field teams, you will make releases predictable and catch failures on the bench, not in the field. What you’ll do Define and evolve a unified onboard service architecture: service boundaries, messaging, configuration, startup ordering, readiness, watchdogs, and graceful degradation when dependencies or devices are unavailable. Build and migrate production services to shared patterns, using reusable libraries and a reference service template covering project structure, packaging, logging, health reporting, and lifecycle management. Standardise local service communication around NATS, with clear rules for integrating MAVLink, ZMQ IPC, and HTTP where appropriate. Design stable, versioned vehicle-to-backend contracts for telemetry, commands and acknowledgements, video metadata and control, configuration, health, and logs. Engineer for unreliable connectivity: buffering and store-and-forward, idempotent commands, explicit acknowledgements and timeouts, reconnection, back-off, and safe behaviour when the backend is unreachable. Implement secure-by-default services: least-privilege identities and messaging permissions, mutually authenticated and encrypted backend links, secure credential provisioning and rotation, sandboxed runtimes, and audit events for safety-critical commands. Strengthen automated testing across unit, contract, integration, simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop tests, with CI gates that catch regressions before release. Build safer release workflows with signed packages, dependency scanning, bench smoke and soak tests, staged fleet rollouts, and reliable rollback. Profile services and enforce practical CPU, memory, and latency budgets on target hardware. Improve field diagnostics through structured logs, metrics, standardised health reporting, post-mission log capture, and actionable runbooks. Document architectural decisions and service interfaces, communicate trade-offs clearly, and use AI coding tools to accelerate delivery without compromising quality. What success looks like Actively developed onboard services converge on a shared architecture, supported Python runtime, messaging model, and service template. Engineers can take a new service from an empty repository to running on a bench vehicle in a day or less, with less duplicated infrastructure code. Vehicle-to-backend contracts remain compatible as cloud and vehicle software evolve at different speeds, preventing integration failures in the field. Authentication, least privilege, secret handling, runtime hardening, and supply-chain checks are consistently applied across the onboard stack. Automated tests and bench validation catch defects before deployment, reducing issues discovered in the field. Releases move predictably from bench validation to pilot vehicles and the wider fleet, with clear readiness gates and rollback procedures. Services stay within resource budgets and remain diagnosable under hardware constraints and degraded connectivity. Architecture documentation and runbooks help engineering, QA, and field teams integrate changes and resolve failures faster. Required Qualifications 10+ years of professional experience in software engineering , delivering and operating production systems. 2+ years as a Tech Lead or Staff Engineer , owning architecture across multiple services or teams and establishing standards adopted by others. Expert Python — designs and ships production services (asyncio, packaging, testing, profiling, and performance); Node.js experience is a plus. Distributed / edge system architecture — has designed service architectures and messaging systems (e.g., NATS, MQTT, ZMQ, Kafka) with versioned contracts across system boundaries and unreliable networks. Web development and API experience — has built and evolved HTTP/WebSocket APIs and message-based integrations for multiple consumers. Security architecture — has led the design of authentication and authorisation, secrets and key management, secure updates, and supply-chain controls; security reviews or certification evidence are a strong plus. Quality engineering leadership — has established test strategies, CI gates, and staged release pipelines for a team or organisation; simulator or hardware-in-the-loop experience is a strong plus. Development with AI tools — uses AI coding assistants or agents daily and has introduced practices that help a team use them effectively and safely. C++, Rust, or Go experience is a plus. UxV, robotics, or embedded/edge Linux experience (e.g., MAVLink, GStreamer, serial/CAN devices, systemd services on constrained hardware) is a plus. The nature of combat has changed. title: Product Support Engineer - EMEA
company: How We Work & What We Value - Ashby
description: Hello! I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. I’m excited to share that we’re hiring a Product Support Engineer in EMEA 🎉 We’re expanding our global Support team to provide 24/7 coverage across time zones. You’ll join a global team while establishing the technical Support Engineering presence in EMEA, with the ownership and visibility that come from being one of the first Support Engineers across European time zones. We staff across regions rather than relying on on-call rotations; we’ll discuss the specific schedule for this opening during the process. Not sure which Support role is right for you? We’re hiring for both Product Support Specialist and Product Support Engineer roles. Support Specialist owns cases and customer communication end-to-end. Troubleshoots complex issues by navigating internal tooling — audit logs, user experience testing, and API testing — to help customers reach successful outcomes. Support Engineering serves as the escalation point between Support Specialists and Product Engineering. Owns integrations, supports data mapping and data migrations for customers, and resolves escalated tickets that don't require product code changes. Please choose the role that best reflects your experience and interests rather than applying to both. If another Support role seems like a closer match, we’ll consider that in our review. About the role Support Engineering is the technical layer between frontline Support and Engineering. You’ll take on complex issues involving integrations, APIs, permissions, data, reporting, migrations, and workflows—using application behavior, logs, databases, and customer context to determine whether an issue can be resolved through Support or represents a product defect. You’ll investigate issues end to end using tools such as Plain, GitHub, Datadog, databases, and the codebase. You won’t write the fix; you’ll give Engineering a well-validated escalation with reproduction steps, relevant evidence, customer impact, and a root-cause hypothesis when possible. You’ll also identify recurring issues, improve documentation and enablement, and partner with Product and Engineering on improvements. As an early Support Engineer in EMEA, you’ll establish regional operating practices and handoff norms across European time zones while bringing EMEA customer patterns to a global team. What you’ll own Own complex technical issues from intake through resolution or escalation—investigating APIs, integrations, logs, data, configuration, and workflows to determine whether Support can resolve them or Engineering should be involved. Set a high bar for complex technical investigations and ensure Engineering receives clear, actionable, well-validated product issues. Build trusted working relationships with frontline Support, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and customers. Identify recurring problems and turn them into documentation, enablement, tooling, process improvements, or product feedback. Partner with Product and Engineering on recurring product improvements by synthesizing customer patterns, validating defects, and sharing the technical context needed to choose between a product change, documentation, tooling, or process improvement. Establish EMEA coverage, handoff, and operating practices across European time zones while bringing regional customer patterns to the global Support Engineering team. Track and improve the outcomes that matter: resolution speed, escalation quality, fewer avoidable Engineering escalations, frontline self-sufficiency, reduced customer effort, and customer confidence. You should apply if: You’ve worked in a hands-on, customer-centric technical role where you independently investigate ambiguous issues involving APIs, integrations, logs, data, and application behavior. You’re comfortable moving between customer conversations, APIs, logs, databases, product behavior, and code-level context to find root causes. You can distinguish a configuration, data, documentation, or enablement issue from a true product defect—and explain your reasoning clearly. You write precise investigations that others can quickly understand and act on, and communicate thoughtfully with technical and non-technical audiences across time zones. You naturally look beyond the immediate ticket and improve the systems around it through documentation, enablement, tooling, or process design. You want to be an early technical owner for EMEA and are energized by building regional structure within a global team. You should not apply if: You’re looking primarily for a high-volume support role centered on predefined troubleshooting steps, rather than open-ended technical investigation and ownership. Most of your experience is in internal IT, help desk, endpoint, hardware, network, infrastructure, cloud operations, systems administration, infrastructure maintenance, or service deployment—and you haven’t worked extensively with customer-centric SaaS applications, APIs, logs, or data-backed troubleshooting. You prefer to pass difficult issues to another team rather than reproduce, investigate, and explain them yourself. You’re looking for a role focused mainly on writing production code; this role diagnoses and escalates bugs but does not own code changes. You prefer clear-cut problems and predefined answers over working through ambiguity with careful documentation, focused questions, and evidence-based decisions. You want a narrowly defined role without regional operating ownership or projects that improve how the broader Support team works. About Ashby Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com . About Go To Market We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us: We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell. We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers. We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Leadership Principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby. Interview process Our interview process is thorough and designed to give you enough information to assess whether Ashby is the right fit for you, while helping us evaluate technical reasoning, communication precision, and ownership. Intro call with Recruiting — 30 min Take-home assessment — 5 days to complete Hiring Manager interview — 45–60 min Virtual onsite — 120 min Meet the team — 30 min Technical & integration skills — 45 min CS and Support leadership — 30 min Closing questions — 15 min Onboarding Your onboarding will combine Ashby-wide product and company training with a Support Engineering-specific ramp plan. You’ll learn the product and support workflow, get familiar with the tools and systems used for technical investigations, and build relationships across Support, Product, and Engineering. With support from your manager and onboarding buddy, you’ll take on increasingly complex investigations as you build context, with regular check-ins throughout your first 90 days. Benefits Benefits vary by country and are shared in more detail during the process. International employees receive statutory benefits and, where available, employer-paid supplemental health coverage. 10-year exercise window for stock options. title: Technical Product Manager
description: About BJAK The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name. Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia. Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you. The Role BJAK is building a Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia. As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it. This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges. We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved. What you'll be doing Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against. Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery. Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back. Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness. Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record. Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears. Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation. What you'll need Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers. Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify. Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control). AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all. Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience. Outcomes Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction Location This role is based in UK . This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our London office at least 3 days per week. Language English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required. Interview Process Our process is designed to move fast: 1. Online assessment or practical task 2. Role-specific interview 3. CEO / final round For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. description: <h2 data-pm-slice="1 1 []">ABOUT BLENHEIM CHALCOT</h2> <p>At Blenheim Chalcot, we invest more than just funds. We invest our knowledge and experience, our ideas and infrastructure.</p> <p>We are a leading digital venture builder, creating and scaling businesses that transform industries through technology, innovation and entrepreneurship.</p> <p>Our ventures operate across a wide range of sectors, including FinTech, EdTech, GovTech, Media and Marketing Technology. Businesses we have built include ClearScore, Salary Finance and Modulr.</p> <p>We provide our portfolio businesses with the expertise, infrastructure and strategic support needed to scale successfully, spanning technology, commercial growth, talent, finance and operations.</p> <p>For graduates, this creates a unique opportunity to gain exposure to entrepreneurial thinking, innovative technologies and the practical challenges of building successful businesses.</p> <h2>ABOUT FOSPHA</h2> <p><strong>Fospha is a fast-growing marketing measurement technology company transforming how global brands understand and optimise their marketing performance.</strong></p> <p>In an increasingly complex digital landscape, Fospha helps businesses understand what is driving growth across their marketing channels, enabling smarter investment decisions and more effective commercial strategies.</p> <p>Combining advanced data science, AI and marketing analytics, Fospha provides a powerful measurement platform that allows brands to understand the full impact of their advertising investments.</p> <p>Working with leading global brands, Fospha is at the forefront of innovation in marketing technology, helping businesses make data-driven decisions and unlock new opportunities for growth.</p> <p>With an international team spanning multiple markets, Fospha offers an exciting environment for ambitious graduates who want to develop their skills, challenge conventional thinking and contribute to a rapidly scaling technology business.</p> <p>Find out more:<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span><a href="https://www.fospha.com/" data-rich-text-autolink="">https://www.fospha.com</a></p> <h2>THE GRADUATE OPPORTUNITY</h2> <p>Joining Blenheim Chalcot as a Graduate, you will gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment while working directly within Fospha.</p> <p>You will be embedded within the Fospha team, contributing to meaningful projects across commercial strategy, business operations, analytics, AI and growth initiatives, depending on business priorities and your strengths.</p> <p>This is not a traditional graduate scheme where you spend months observing. From the outset, you will be encouraged to take ownership, contribute ideas and make a measurable impact.</p> <p>For you as a graduate, this opportunity involves:</p> <ul data-spread="true"> <li> <p><strong>Dedicated to Fospha</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>– Although you will be employed by Blenheim Chalcot, your day-to-day responsibilities, projects and objectives will be focused on supporting Fospha's growth and strategic priorities.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Commercial & Strategic Exposure</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>– Gain experience working on real business challenges, analysing opportunities, improving processes and supporting initiatives that contribute directly to business performance.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>AI, Data & Technology</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>– Develop practical experience of how AI, automation and data-driven decision-making can transform business operations, enhance productivity and create commercial value.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Training & Development</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>– Access Blenheim Chalcot's learning and development opportunities, designed to strengthen your professional, commercial, analytical and leadership skills.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Early Careers Development</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>– Benefit from structured development opportunities, mentoring and exposure to experienced professionals across Fospha and the wider BC portfolio.</p> </li> <li> opportunities, collaborative projects and social events.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Accountability & Ownership</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>– Take responsibility for meaningful scale.</p> </li> </ul> <h2>WHAT YOU COULD BE WORKING ON</h2> <p>Depending on your interests, capabilities and Fospha's business priorities, you could be involved in:</p> <ul data-spread="false"> <li> <p>Analysing commercial performance, market opportunities and business growth initiatives.</p> </li> <li> <p>Supporting strategic projects that improve operational efficiency and scalability.</p> </li> <li> <p>Exploring how AI tools and automation can improve existing business processes.</p> </li> <li> <p>Working with stakeholders across commercial, product, operations and analytics teams.</p> </li> <li> <p>Conducting research, preparing business cases and presenting recommendations to senior stakeholders.</p> </li> <li> <p>Identifying opportunities to improve how the business operates, makes decisions and delivers value to customers.</p> </li> <li> <p>Supporting cross-functional initiatives within a fast-growing international technology business.</p> </li> </ul> <p>We are looking for graduates who are excited by the opportunity to get involved in different challenges, learn quickly and contribute wherever they can make the biggest impact.</p> <h2>ARE YOU BC?</h2> <p>We don't expect you to have worked in a start-up before, studied a technology-related degree or have extensive professional experience.</p> <p>We are more interested in your potential, mindset and ability to learn.</p> <p>We welcome applications from graduates across all academic disciplines, particularly those who demonstrate strong analytical thinking, intellectual curiosity, commercial awareness and an interest in technology.</p> <p>We look for some key fundamentals in people joining the BC Group:</p> <ul data-spread="true"> <li> <p><strong>Curious</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>– You ask questions, challenge assumptions and are always looking for better ways of doing things. We're now looking for a Design Engineer who wants to design & ship exceptional outcomes for users. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating. We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates. We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have grown the team 3x and revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, are launching an end-to-end solar and battery product in November, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. Day-to-day you'll be: Designing and shipping – You'll take a flow from rough idea all the way to production, prototyping in whatever gets you to an answer fastest (often code, sometimes Figma or a sketch), and testing with installers as you go. The gap between "we should fix this" and "it's fixed" is often a day. Owning the interaction layer – You'll build and look after the component library and the patterns underneath it: motion, loading and empty states, touch targets that still work with gloves on. The small things that make a complex tool feel simple. Building the parts that are hard to get right – The canvas-based floor plan and system design tools, the offline survey app (incl. LiDAR), the proposals homeowners see. These are the parts where the UI is the product, and where we've got the most still to build. Raising the bar on everything we ship – You'll work closely with our product designers and developers, pairing on their work and reviewing it, so the quality of what you build rubs off on the rest of the product. Spending time with installers – You'll go out on site, watch how the product actually gets used, then come back and change it. You'll report to Steph , our co-founder and CPO (she’s pretty awesome) and you’ll work alongside Dan & Arron who’ve cooked up some incredible work in their time so far. 🫵 About you We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft. You might currently call yourself a designer who ships, a front-end engineer with strong design instincts, or already a design engineer. We're looking for 3+ years of experience (and potentially a lot more) designing and building product UI, ideally in a startup or a fast-paced, impact-focussed team. We'd love to speak with you if you have: Real taste, and shipped work to prove it – You can show us production UI you designed and built, and talk about why the details are the way they are. Work you'd happily put next to the best-crafted B2B products out there. Strong design craft, and a real appetite for code – You're a strong designer first. You don't need to be a front-end engineer, and you might well ship with Cursor or Claude Code, but you want to understand the code you're shipping. Bonus for React and TypeScript depth, canvas/WebGL, animation, or complex state on mobile. A prototyping instinct – You'd rather build a rough version and test it than argue about it in a doc. You're comfortable with things being imperfect in front of users. Systems thinking – You enjoy the structure of a good component library and understand that consistency is what lets a small team ship fast. You also know when to slow down first: you value time spent on lo-fi wireframes and on understanding the data model before anything gets polished. Curiosity about the domain – You want to understand how heating systems, solar and battery actually work, and you pick up technical detail fast. By the end of week two you'll be arguing about the best way to show a homeowner their solar self-consumption. 🌟 Our offer 💰 £60-110k salary, depending on experience and location 🍰 Meaningful slice of equity (options) in the company 🏖️ 33 days holiday (25 plus bank holidays) and opportunity to work from abroad for another 30 days each year 🏡 Hybrid working: 2–3 days in-person a week (London or Bristol), with full-team meetups every fortnight 🏥 Private Medical Cover (Vitality) 👧 Workplace Nursery Benefit scheme ( YellowNest ) 🧑‍🍼 Enhanced Parental Leave 🚲 Cycle to Work scheme 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Brilliant team to learn from and massive opportunity to grow 🧑‍💻 Working at Spruce We're currently a close-knit team of 34, split between London and Bristol. We spend 2-3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone together every fortnight. You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense. We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then be able to rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions. This is clearly particularly important for this role but you'll be surrounded by a whole team who are also close to our customers. We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. When things break, we focus on how we fix it, what we can learn, and never blame. title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, LLM Inference Optimization
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>About Nebius:</strong></p> <p>Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.</p> <p>Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.</p> <p>Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.</p></div><h2>The role</h2> <p>As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer on the Applied AI team at Nebius Token Factory, you will own model and endpoint optimization from model artifacts through production deployment. Your work will span model internals, quantization and model compression, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, inference engines, serving architecture, and benchmarking to improve latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, and cost per token while preserving quality and reliability.</p> <p>You will work with kernel and platform engineers to investigate serving problems, compare configurations, and resolve performance and quality regressions. You will evaluate model- and engine-level optimizations together with distributed inference designs, including request routing, scheduling, prefill/decode coordination, and multi-node GPU execution. Your improvements will be validated through reproducible benchmarks and safe production rollouts under real-world workloads.</p> <h2>Your responsibilities</h2> <ul> <li>Own optimization projects for specific model families, customer endpoints, or serving backends.</li> <li>Compare inference engines and recommend serving configurations suited to individual workloads.</li> <li>Diagnose model-quality and performance regressions during production rollouts.</li> <li>Improve LLM and VLM endpoint latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, quality, and cost per token.</li> <li>Deploy, configure, benchmark, and extend engines such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo.</li> <li>Develop production model-compression workflows covering quantization, quantization-aware training, distillation, low-bit serving, and accuracy recovery.</li> <li>Implement or integrate speculative decoding, draft-model approaches, KV-cache optimization, prefix caching, chunked prefill, continuous batching, and disaggregated prefill/decode serving. For prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD), evaluate KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and capacity balancing to determine which workloads benefit from the architecture.</li> <li>Design and improve LLM request routers and scheduling policies that balance worker utilization, queueing, request characteristics, and KV-cache locality while meeting latency and reliability targets.</li> <li>Scale dense and mixture-of-experts inference across multiple GPU nodes. Select and tune tensor, pipeline, data, and expert parallelism—including wide expert parallelism (WideEP)—with attention to hardware topology, expert load balance, and communication overhead.</li> <li>Build reproducible benchmark harnesses measuring TTFT, TPOT, tokens per second per GPU, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory, reliability, and cost per token. Validate architecture choices under representative traffic and consistent GPU budgets.</li> <li>Collaborate with GPU kernel and platform engineers to trace bottlenecks across model code, kernels, runtime, scheduler, gateway, and cluster layers.</li> <li>Produce design documents, performance reports, rollout plans, and customer-facing technical explanations.</li> </ul> <h2>Must-haves</h2> <ul> <li>Strong engineering skills in Python and PyTorch.</li> <li>Hands-on experience deploying or optimizing LLM, VLM, or high-throughput transformer inference.</li> <li>Practical knowledge of at least one modern inference stack, such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA Dynamo, Ray Serve, KServe, or an equivalent internal system.</li> <li>A strong understanding of transformer inference bottlenecks involving KV cache, attention, memory bandwidth, batching, parallelism, and long-context serving.</li> <li>Ability to quantify trade-offs among latency, throughput, quality, utilization, and cost.</li> <li>Experience designing or optimizing distributed inference system architecture, with hands-on work in one or more areas such as request routing, distributed scheduling, PDD, multi-node inference, or expert parallelism.</li> <li>Strong communication and collaboration skills across research, kernel, infrastructure, product, and customer teams.</li> </ul> <h2>Nice-to-haves</h2> <ul> <li>Experience title: Software Engineer
description: <h3>About the Position</h3> <p>Our goal is to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street full time while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. As an intern, you are paired with full-time employees who act as mentors, collaborating with you on real-world projects we actually need done.</p> <p>As a Software Engineering intern, you'll learn how we use OCaml (our primary development language) in our day-to-day work, and gain exposure to the libraries and tools that are foundational to our internal systems. Some teams also use Python, so depending on the project, you might do some work with Python as well.</p> <p>During the internship, you'll be closely mentored by full-time software engineers. Mentors design intern projects based on their team's current needs and are heavily invested in helping interns build maintainable, high-quality software that is intended to reach production. The projects you will work on are as varied and diverse as those full-timers work on, covering a wide range of problems, from high-performance trading systems to programming language design and everything in between.</p> <p>If you’d like to learn more, you can read about our <a href="https://www.janestreet.com/preparing-for-a-software-engineering-interview/">interview</a> and<a href="https://blog.janestreet.com/project-pairing/#fn:1"> team placement</a> processes and get a sense of what our <a href="https://blog.janestreet.com/tag/internship/">most recent intern projects</a> looked like! You can also learn more about Jane Street’s internship program <a href="https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/internships/">here</a>.</p> <h3>About You</h3> <p>If you've never thought about a career in finance, you're in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind, a collaborative spirit, and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you'll fit right in. We're more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:</p> <ul> <li>A top-notch programmer with a love for technology</li> <li>Intellectually curious, collaborative, and eager to learn</li> <li>Humble and unafraid to ask questions and admit mistakes</li> <li>Fluent in English</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p> </p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

Demonstrated experience holding clinical standards across multiple sites or a large clinical team. Preferred Experience in preventive care, tech enabled healthcare or longitudinal care models. Partner directly with engineering and architecture teams to design controls into new systems at build time and translate that technical work into the narratives auditors actually need. Partner with the Security Compliance Manager to shape and mature the global compliance program. Design, implement and validate security controls relevant to DoorDash's regulatory environment, not just document them. Support development and refinement of security policies, standards, and guidance. Mentor other members of the compliance team and help set the technical bar the rest of the function grows into. Ensure policies are actionable, testable, and aligned to real-world controls. We're excited about you because you have… 5+ years of experience in security compliance, GRC or technology risk, with a strong track record in high-growth, technology-driven and regulated environments. Hands-on experience building large language models and agent workflows with daily use of AI in your own work, grounded judgment on what to delegate to agents versus what needs a human, and the ability to evidence both to an auditor. DoorDash is an AI-forward organization and the ability to optimize efficiency using AI is crucial in this role. The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience with frameworks such as DORA, the EU AI Act, NIS2 and CRA. Real, hands-on experience implementing and assessing controls against frameworks like PCI DSS, SOC 2, ISO 27001 - not just reading them. Demonstrated ability to identify control gaps, assess risk and drive remediation in partnership with cross-functional stakeholders. Experience developing, implementing and improving security policies, standards, and procedures, ensuring they are operational and effective. Strong understanding of compliance metrics and reporting, with the ability to track control effectiveness, audit outcomes, and risk exposure. Ability to influence and drive accountability across technical and non-technical stakeholders. Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to translate complex audit and compliance requirements into clear, actionable guidance. Comfort owning compliance metrics and reporting - you can show, not just assert, that a program is working. Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Computer Science, or related field, or equivalent practical experience. title: AI Platform Engineer
description: About us People assume the supply chain is an automated, algorithmic system. It is not. It is a large number of people acting as the glue between organisations and systems, doing work the world depends on with tools that have barely changed in decades. Nexcade builds AI agents for those people, starting in freight forwarding, a $210BN industry. Our agents are live in production with some of the leading global forwarders, pricing millions in freight every week, and we are expanding the platform deeper into the shipment lifecycle. We have raised $8.5M to make this a reality. Our founders, Dan and Tasho, spent years at Sedna and Palantir working with supply chain companies on problems like this one. We are backed by top VCs and angels who backed or founded Synthesia, n8n and other world-class companies. How we work Everybody codes, founders included. The whole company is technical, commercial team included, and runs on coding agents. Closely with customers and design partners, so what we ship changes how they operate. At pace. Fast cycles and quick iterations, on the product and on how we work. End to end. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom (and the responsibility) to fix it. In person, 4+ days a week in London. We value synchronous communication. Debate rigorously, decide quickly, execute relentlessly. Enjoy the journey. Hard problems, good colleagues. The role We are building the AI platform for freight forwarding and expanding our product surface, and we are hiring software engineers across product, AI and platform to do it. You will build products that do freight forwarding work alongside our customers' teams, operating across the entire shipment lifecycle. You will work across the stack in Python, TypeScript and React, and directly with customers and founders on what gets built. Everyone here works across the stack, but each engineer has a spike: the area where they set the bar for the team. You spend most of your time where yours is, and lean on your colleagues where theirs are. Product: You build best in class products for the core jobs in freight forwarding, one job at a time. You work as a design partner with our customers to understand the work deeply, turn that understanding into a product they would choose over anything else, and feed what you learn back into the platform everyone builds on. AI: You raise the ceiling on what our AI can do and the floor on how reliably it does it. That spans high volume tasks like classification and extraction and deep workflow tasks that run for hours. You design for performance, reliability, explainability and control, set up the gyms and evals to measure them, and build the harness that runs our agents in all of our products. Platform: You own the foundation every product stands on: the runtime for thousands of concurrent agents and workflows, the way they communicate and scale, the controls for how they access data with permissions that hold, and the observability to see and measure all of it. You ensure the rest of the team can move fast without fear. What we look for A spike, with evidence. Something you have been exceptional at and proof of it. We hire on slope rather than years, so there is no experience threshold in either direction. Strong fundamentals. In the AI-assisted era, having good technical judgement is key. You have shipped production systems people depend on, seen them fail and learned from it. High agency and ownership. You take an ambiguous problem, make a call, and see it through. Humility and learning velocity. You want to get better and you change your mind when the evidence says so. Interest in the problem. You do not need a freight background, but you need to find messy real-world operations interesting rather than a chore. Why join You will shape the product, the architecture and the company, working alongside an engineering team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will work directly with the businesses using what you build, on AI applied to an industry that has resisted software for decades. You will get meaningful equity, so when this works you share in it. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Product Marketing Manager - Care Providers & Health
description: Finance Deserves Better Finance teams at fast-growing companies run global, real-time businesses on a patchwork of legacy ERPs and point solutions. Every new entity, site or tool adds another system to stitch together and another hire to keep the numbers reconciled. Light gives them a way out. We build the finance solution that lets finance teams have it all, through three parts that work as one: Our ledger records every transaction across every entity in real time, so the numbers hold up from day one. Our apps adapt Light to how each business runs, from procurement to billing to reporting. Our agents operate the repetitive work that used to need another hire, so finance teams spend their time on the decisions that matter. Today we run the finance function for companies like Lovable, Legora and Keyshot, with backing from Atomico, Balderton, Seedcamp, Cherry and Entrée. Now we’re taking Light into specific industries, with the ambition of becoming the operating layer each one runs on. Care homes and clinics sit among our priority sectors. The Role We’re looking for a Product Marketing Manager to go deep on health, starting with groups that run several care homes, clinics or practices, and work out how Light wins there. These groups carry the finance problems of any multi-entity business, plus funding models, regulation and workflows of their own. Your job is to understand these buyers better than anyone at Light, turn what you learn into positioning and proof our sales team can use, and build the playbook we follow to scale our go-to-market across the sector. You’ll sit in our product marketing team and work side by side with our Care and Health Sales Managers, with support from demand generation, field marketing and product. What You’ll Be Doing Interviewing customers, prospects and specialist partners to learn how care home groups and clinics buy, what makes them change and where their finance workflows break. Mapping the market with Sales: which segments we go after first, which we test, and which we leave for later. Turning what you learn into positioning, messaging and competitive arguments that hold up in front of an operator or a finance director. Building the sales kit, from customer stories and demo narratives to objection handling and one-pagers, so our reps speak the sector’s language. Training sales reps and SDRs on the buyers, workflows and vocabulary of each segment, and joining customer calls to hear what lands. Bringing the sector’s requirements back to Product, and separating the needs that recur from the one-off requests. Giving demand generation and field marketing the insight, content and angles they need for sector campaigns and events, and tracking what turns into pipeline. Writing down what works, so the next sector we enter starts from a playbook rather than a blank page. What We Think* You’ll Need Product marketing experience at a B2B SaaS company, with a track record of taking a product or segment from insight to launch to sales adoption. A habit of talking to customers, and the judgement to turn interviews into clear positioning. Experience in health, care or a closely related sector helps. Curiosity and the speed to earn credibility with operators matter more. Strong writing, from a sharp one-pager to a customer story people want to share. Comfort working with Sales every day, and a feel for what helps a rep win a deal. An analytical streak. You can read funnel data, spot where deals stall and test why. Daily use of AI for research, writing and analysis, with the discipline to check what it tells you. A can-do, empathetic and collaborative spirit. No brilliant jerks here, please. *If the core of the role sounds compelling but you don’t tick every box, we’d still love for you to reach out and convince us you’re the right person. The Good Stuff 🏢 A five-day, in-office culture with a high-density team in London. 💸 A competitive salary and potential stock options. 🏝 25 days of annual leave plus UK public holidays. 🥳 Regular socials and two company offsites a year. The last 2 were in Tuscany & Provence! 🌍 Travel to Copenhagen, Munich, New York, Paris and wherever care homes and clinics do business. 🚀 The chance to define how Light wins in a sector from its first deals. Light is an equal opportunity employer. The Famous Last Words Care home groups and clinics run complex businesses on finance tools that weren’t built for them. We want to change that, and we want you to learn the sector inside out and show us how. When you apply, tell us about a segment you got to know from scratch: how you learned it, what you changed because of it, and how you helped Sales win there. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Product Manager
description: Product Manager, Lead to Cash Location: London, onsite 5 days a week Retire The ERP. Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers: automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business. We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Keyshot. We’re an early team defining a new software category. If you’re excited to modernise how the world runs money, one agentic workflow at a time, you’re in the right place. Backed by world-class investors and advised by industry titans, we’re building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance. About The Role This is a hands-on product role reporting to the VP of Product Development. You’ll own Lead to Cash: everything between a signed deal and cash in the bank. That covers contracts, billing and invoicing, revenue recognition, payments, and credit control. You’ll set the roadmap for the area with the VP, and your discovery and judgement decide what actually ships. In Lead to Cash, the ledger has to keep up with whatever commercial terms each customer signs. A contract changes mid-term, and the invoices, deferred revenue and reporting all have to follow. A parent company wants one bill for a dozen subsidiaries. A customer’s Stripe setup doesn’t match how they actually sell. Every customer bills a little differently, and the product has to absorb those differences without turning into a pile of one-offs. You work out which problems are patterns worth building for and which aren’t, and you say so. Your stakeholders are engineers, designers, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Implementation, and the Financial Controllers, Finance Directors and CFOs who run their revenue on Light. Most of them are senior, technical and short of time. They expect you to keep up, and to be honest with them when a request would cost more than it’s worth. Key Responsibilities Own the Lead to Cash roadmap and its delivery, from discovery to go-live, and the metrics that show whether it’s working for customers Turn contract terms, pricing models and revenue recognition rules into product requirements engineers can build from Decide which customer requests become product and which don’t, and bring a clear recommendation to the VP of Product Development when the call is a big one Lead discovery with finance teams: sit with them through a billing run or a month-end close and find what’s slow, manual or wrong Work with Sales and Solutions Engineering on what gets promised to customers, before it’s promised Sequence delivery with Engineering and Design without cutting the corners that matter in finance Own the integrations that feed Lead to Cash, such as CRMs and payment providers, with clear scope for each Spot a release going off-track before it slips, and escalate or intervene early Enable the teams downstream of you (Sales, SE, Implementation, Support) to sell, set up and support every Lead to Cash feature from day one Shape how AI agents run billing and collections work, inside policies that finance teams set and can audit Experience & Qualifications* We’re looking for someone with around 4–8 years in product (or equivalent experience), who brings: You ship product, not slideware. You’ve owned real features that real users depend on. You measure yourself by what went live and what it changed, not by the roadmap you maintained. This is the non-negotiable. You turn accounting rules into product. You can read IFRS 15 or ASC 606, a customer’s master services agreement, or a messy pricing sheet and work out what the product has to do. You know why a mid-term upgrade, a backdated discount or an early termination breaks a simple billing model, and you design for it before a customer finds it. You know revenue. You understand order-to-cash in practice: contracts, billing schedules, deferred and recognised revenue, credit notes, dunning, and matching cash against invoices. You can talk confidently with a Controller about how revenue should land in the books. An accounting qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA or local equivalent) is a strong plus, and so is time spent running billing or revenue operations yourself. You can say no, explain why, and keep the relationship intact. Lead to Cash attracts customer-specific requests, and many arrive already promised. You can tell a pattern from a one-off, explain the cost of each to Sales and to customers, and turn the patterns into product that serves the next customer as well as this one. You’re AI-native. You’ve changed the way you work because of AI tooling, not just added it to your workflow. You use it to read contracts and pricing models, prototype, draft specs and pressure-test your own thinking, and you have an instinct for where it helps, where it misleads, and how to use it without losing ownership of the outcome. You own discovery. You talk to customers directly and often: their finance teams, the people who run their billing, and our own Sales and Implementation teams who set them up. You can tell the difference between what a customer asks for and the problem underneath it, and you turn that into the smallest thing worth building next. You deliver through other people. You’ve shipped through Product, Engineering, Design and Sales without formal authority over any of them. You build trust with senior finance stakeholders through clear communication and consistent delivery. Fluent English; additional European languages a plus. *If the core of the role sounds compelling but you don’t tick every box, we’d still love for you to reach out and convince us you’re the right person. Bonus Points Experience building billing, subscription or revenue recognition products, or running billing at a SaaS company Familiarity with billing and payment platforms such as Stripe, Chargebee or Zuora, and CRMs such as HubSpot or Salesforce Experience in fintech or systems where data integrity is non-negotiable Experience with usage-based, tiered or hybrid pricing models Background in high-growth startups where everything was still being figured out Familiarity with multi-currency, multi-entity billing and e-invoicing mandates (e.g. Peppol, Italy’s SDI) You’ll Probably Struggle Here If You need a finished spec handed to you. Here the “requirement” is often a contract clause or a pricing sheet nobody has turned into product yet. You need a PMO, a mature methodology or a big delivery org around you to operate. This is a startup environment, and ownership and a self-starter nature are key. You treat every customer request as a commitment. The job is deciding which ones become product. You find it hard to say no to a customer or colleague, even when it’s the right call. You haven’t yet changed how you work because of AI. We go all in on AI at Light and want people who share that. Our Tech Stack We build on AWS, with a Kotlin backend, a React frontend, and infrastructure managed in Terraform. It’s a real production system that global finance teams depend on every day. You won’t be writing the code, but you’ll live alongside it. You do need to be comfortable in this kind of environment: real scale, real customers, real stakes. The Good Stuff In addition to being part of a great team and working in a fun and innovative environment, we offer: 💸 A competitive salary and potential stock options. 🏝 A generous paid annual leave package, plus UK public holidays. 🥳 Regular socials and two company offsites a year. The last 2 were in Tuscany & Provence! 🚀 A huge opportunity for career growth as you help shape a market-defining product. Light is an equal opportunity employer. The Famous Last Words Working at Light means you’re embarking on an exciting journey to reshape the future of multinational financial operations. Our cheat code is that we’ve built something like this before, and now we’re doing it again, only better. Our goal is to make global finance effortless and empower companies to make informed decisions. Join the rocket ship while it’s taking off 🚀 Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow
